issues.description: The specification and UML define the domain entity as class "Meal" (used for orders in SealSaloon), but the template instead provides a class named "Order" with the same conceptual role (name + ingredients) while Meal.java is empty. This naming mismatch forces students to reconcile two competing concepts and will likely cause compilation/test failures where APIs expect Meal.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the starter code to the spec by renaming/removing Order.java and providing Meal.java (class Meal with fields name/ingredients, constructor, and getters). Update Main and any starter references to use Meal consistently.

issues.description: The specification is internally inconsistent about the SealSaloon field "stock": it first describes it as an instance field "final Stock stock" initialized in the constructor, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). Students cannot implement both an instance final field and a shared static field without clarification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (a) state and diagram "static final Stock stock" (shared) or (b) remove the static requirement and keep "final Stock stock" per instance. Update the UML accordingly (mark stock as {static} if shared).
